angle: In London and the snowbelt towns around it, a hot tub or sauna is what you use at the end of a twelve hour shift at the hospital, after shovelling lake-effect snow in Strathroy, or under the maples of a Byron backyard in October when the leaves are coming down.

hot-tub.intro: The Forest City has the yards for it: deep lots under mature maples, new builds in the south and northwest, and hospital and campus schedules that make a nightly soak a habit. Red Tag pricing takes 20% off every new 2026 Jacuzzi in stock.
body: London's mature neighbourhoods, Byron, Old South, Oakridge and Westmount among them, sit under one of the biggest urban tree canopies in Ontario, and that changes how you own a tub. Leaves, maple keys and seed pods land on the cover from September through November, so a cover lifter and a quick brush-off become part of the routine, and a tub placed just outside the drip line stays cleaner than one tucked under the branches. Deep shade also keeps the vinyl from baking in July, which is one reason covers on treed lots here tend to outlast the ones on open subdivision lots.

West and north of the city the snow arrives differently. Strathroy, Komoka, Lucan and Ilderton sit in the band that catches lake-effect streamers off Lake Huron, so a January out there can mean a foot of fresh snow on the cover several times a week. Every tub we deliver into the snowbelt leaves with a well fitted, high density cover, and we walk you through where to place it so the west wind does not drive snow into the equipment bay. Full foam Jacuzzi shells and the insulated Wellness Shop Ontario series hold their heat when the temperature sits below minus ten for a stretch.

Who is buying? Nurses and residents from LHSC and St. Joseph's who get home at odd hours, Western and Fanshawe staff, families in the new phases of Summerside, Talbot Village and Hyde Park, and farm households out toward Dorchester and Ingersoll with room for anything. A J-335 or J-355 suits a couple on a Westmount lot, a J-408 or J-509 suits a household of six in a new build with a walkout, and a Nordic Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 suits a rural garage or a first tub. Our London crews handle every delivery, and most city lots take a dolly through the side gate.

faq.q: How do I keep leaves and maple keys out of the tub on a treed lot in Byron or Old South?
faq.a: Keep the cover on whenever the tub is not in use and add a cover lifter so it is never dragged across the deck. Sweep the cover with a soft brush before you open it, and set a filter cycle to run after you close up in the evening. A tub placed a few feet outside the drip line of a maple collects far less debris than one directly beneath it.

faq.q: Will lake-effect snow west of London be a problem for the cover?
faq.a: The cover is built to carry a normal load, but repeated heavy dumps in Strathroy, Lucan or Ilderton should be brushed off rather than left to sit and turn to ice. Push snow toward the hinge side with a foam brush, never a shovel edge. If a storm drops more than a foot, clear it the same day, because wet snow that freezes overnight is what bows a cover.

faq.q: Does it cost more to heat a tub in a Strathroy winter than in the city?
faq.a: A little, and mostly because of wind rather than temperature. A tub on an exposed rural lot loses more heat through the cover seam than one behind a fence in Westmount, so placement near the house or a windbreak matters more out there than the model does. Full foam insulation and a cover that seals well are the two things that keep the hydro bill flat from November to March.

faq.q: Should I fill from the well or truck in water for a rural tub near Ingersoll or Dorchester?
faq.a: Most rural customers fill from the well and it works fine once a metal sequestering product goes in on fill day. Iron and hardness are the usual issues in Oxford and Middlesex wells, so bring a sample to the showroom and we will test it before delivery. If the well runs low in late summer, a water hauler can fill a full size tub quickly and some owners prefer that for the first fill.

faq.q: Where should the tub go on a new build in south or northwest London?
faq.a: Most new lots in Summerside, Talbot Village and Hyde Park are graded to drain toward the rear swale, so the pad needs to sit level on compacted base rather than on fresh fill that will settle. Keep the tub within a reasonable run of the panel to hold down the electrical cost, and check with the city on setbacks from the property line before the concrete goes in. If the fence is going in the same season, leave the gate at least three feet wide for the dolly.

swim-spa.intro: Swim spas make sense where the yard is big and the swim season is short. A heated lane that stays open through a London February appeals to triathletes training for summer, to physiotherapy patients, and to families who want a pool without the fall shutdown.
body: London has the lot sizes for a swim spa. Established streets in Byron, Oakridge and Old North have deep rear yards where a 14 or 16 foot spa sits comfortably with room for a deck, and rural properties around Dorchester, Ilderton and Lucan can take a 19 foot model with the truck backing straight to the pad and no crane in the picture. In the newer south and northwest subdivisions the yards are shallower, so the 12 foot J-12 Flow at $30,695 and the 13 foot J-13 PowerPlay at $33,195 are the ones that fit without swallowing the whole lawn.

The people asking about swim spas here are a specific group: masters swimmers and triathletes who train at Western or the city pools, runners and cyclists working through an injury, and staff from the hospitals and Fanshawe who want low impact exercise at home on a shift schedule. For serious swimmers the 16 and 19 foot PowerPro models carry the strongest current. For families and mixed use, the J-19DT PowerPro at $60,895 or the SwimLife SwimExpert DualStream 19 at $56,095 pair a cool swim end with a separate hot tub end, so the kids swim while the adults soak.

Winter is where a swim spa earns its price in this region. Snow off Lake Huron and the long grey stretch from December to March close outdoor pools for half the year, but a covered swim spa runs every day of it. Our crews set most spas on a reinforced concrete pad, and partial in-ground installs are common on sloped ravine lots in Byron and along the Thames where the grade does half the work. We book and manage the crane, and on tight city lots we plan the lift from the street or the driveway before you commit to a model.

faq.q: Can a crane reach a rear yard on a mature street in Old South or Byron?
faq.a: In most cases yes, but the trees decide it. Our installer visits first to find a lift path between the maples and over the roofline, and where the canopy is too dense we look at coming in from a side street or a neighbour's driveway with permission. A spa can also be walked in on rollers where there is a straight, level run and a gate wide enough.

faq.q: How solid does a pad need to be for a 19 foot swim spa on London clay?
faq.a: Southwestern Ontario clay holds water and heaves in a freeze, so a swim spa pad here is usually a reinforced slab poured on a compacted granular base rather than a thin patio pour. Your contractor sizes it for the filled weight of the spa, which runs to several tonnes on a 19 foot model. We supply the footprint and weight figures for whichever model you choose so the pad is right the first time.

faq.q: Is a swim spa a good fit for physiotherapy or a knee rehab?
faq.a: Many of our London swim spa buyers are recovering from surgery or an injury and want warm water walking, jogging against a gentle current, and jetted seats afterward. The PowerActive models let you turn the current down to a walking pace, and the dual temperature DT models keep the swim end cooler than the therapy seats. Talk to your physiotherapist about the routine and we will match the model to it.

faq.q: Which swim spa works for a family on a Dorchester or Ilderton lot with a lot of room?
faq.a: With a rural lot there is no reason to compromise on length, so a J-19 PowerActive at $51,395 or the SwimExpert AquaStream 17 at $50,095 gives the adults a real swim and the kids a pool. The eight seat J-13 PowerPlay is the pick when it is more about soaking and splashing than laps. Delivery to a rural property is usually straight off the truck with no crane needed.

faq.q: How long does it take a swim spa to warm back up after a cold snap?
faq.a: A covered swim spa loses little overnight, so most owners set a temperature and leave it. If you let it drop while you are away, count on the better part of a day to come back up, faster on the 12 and 14 foot models than on a 19 footer. Holding a steady temperature through a Strathroy or Sarnia cold snap costs less than reheating from cold.

sauna.intro: Between shift work at the hospitals, training schedules at Western and long grey winters, London has taken to saunas in a serious way. Clearlight infrared cabins go into basements from Westmount to Masonville, and Serenity cedar saunas go on rural lots with room to breathe.
body: The infrared buyer in London is often someone on a schedule: a nurse or resident who gets home at seven in the morning and wants twenty minutes of heat before sleep, a Western athlete or Fanshawe student working through an injury, or a couple in a Byron bungalow who converted the spare room. The Clearlight Sanctuary 1 at $10,495 fits a corner of a finished basement, and the Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 and Sanctuary 3 at $12,995 handle two or three people, and adding a Chill Tubs Essential turns the basement into a full contrast setup.

Outdoor cedar saunas are a rural London thing. Farm properties around Dorchester, Ilderton, Lucan and Ingersoll have the space, the privacy and often a woodpile, so a Serenity Sauna at $17,495 with a wood-burning heater is a natural fit and needs no electrical run to the far end of the yard. On a treed lot in Byron or a lakeshore property in Sarnia, the Serenity Mini at $14,995 tucks into a corner of the garden. Heaters are sold separately on both, the knotty cedar price is the one shown, and clear cedar is available if you prefer a cleaner grain.

Placement matters in this climate. An outdoor sauna wants a level base, a gravel apron so snowmelt runs away from the sill, and a door that does not face the prevailing westerly. Indoors, a Clearlight needs a dry room with a little clearance around the cabin, and because basements in the older neighbourhoods can be damp, a dehumidifier nearby is a sensible addition. Both types are set up and heated at our Southdale Road West showroom so you can sit inside for ten minutes before you decide.

faq.q: Can I fit a Clearlight in an older London basement with a low ceiling?
faq.a: Many pre-1970 houses in Old South, Old East and Byron have basements under seven feet, so ceiling height is the first thing to measure. Bring the number to the showroom and we will tell you which Sanctuary cabins clear it with room for the roof panel. Where a full cabin will not fit, a corner of the garage or a main floor spare room is the usual answer.

faq.q: Where should a wood-burning Serenity go on a farm lot near Lucan or Dorchester?
faq.a: Give it a level gravel or slab base away from the barn and any stored feed or fuel, with the chimney clear of overhanging branches. A spot within a short walk of the back door gets used on a January night, while one at the far end of the property does not. Check with your township about setbacks and any rules on wood-burning appliances before you build.

faq.q: How does a sauna help with night shifts?
faq.a: Warming up and then cooling down before bed helps a lot of people fall asleep, which is why so many hospital staff in London use an infrared cabin after a night shift. Twenty to thirty minutes at a moderate setting, then a cool shower or a few minutes in a Chill Tub, then bed. Put the cabin on a timer so it is warm when you walk in the door.

faq.q: Is cedar the right choice for humid London summers?
faq.a: Western red cedar handles humidity and temperature swings well, which is why it is the standard for outdoor saunas across Ontario. Leave the vents open between sessions so the interior dries out, and expect the exterior to silver over a few seasons unless you oil it. A gravel apron around the base keeps splash and leaf litter off the bottom boards.

faq.q: Indoor or outdoor if I have a small Westmount or Byron lot?
faq.a: On a mature lot the trees and the neighbours decide. A Serenity Mini fits most side or rear gardens and looks at home under a maple, but if the only spot is close to a fence line, check the setback with the city first. A Clearlight in the basement avoids the question entirely and assembles in a few hours.

hot-tub.small: For a couple in a Westmount or Byron bungalow, a downtown lot with a narrow gate, or a rural garage with limited hydro, the small tubs earn their place. The Jacuzzi J-315 seats three with 23 jets at $18,795 and the J-215 does a similar job at $14,095. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V at $7,295 and Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 plug into a standard outlet, which suits a shop or a beach lot near Port Stanley or Grand Bend where running a new circuit is a project in itself. Aquasolus The Brook, four seats at $10,995, includes White Glove delivery and setup.
hot-tub.medium: Five and six seat tubs are the London sweet spot: two adults, two kids and room for friends on a Friday night after Boler Mountain. The Jacuzzi J-335 at $21,995 and J-355 at $24,795 are the two we sell most on established lots, the J-435 and J-445 at $27,895 step up to J-400 styling and more jets, and the J-408L and J-508L put a lounger in a six seater. On a budget, the J-275 clears from $14,695 while 2025 stock lasts, and the Wellness Shop Ontario L S103 at $15,595 gives you 51 jets and two 6-HP jet pumps.
hot-tub.large: Seven seats and up is a big family in a new build or a rural household that hosts. The Jacuzzi J-509 seats eight with 76 jets at $39,595 and is the tub for a walkout in Sunningdale or a farm lot outside Ingersoll. The J-495 seats nine at $34,595, and the 2025 floor model is $31,395. Further down, the J-385 at $26,595, the J-285 at $18,695 and the J-245 at $16,295 all seat seven, and the Wellness Shop Ontario S106 at $17,695 gives you 59 jets for the price of a mid range J-200. Aquasolus The Cove seats seven at $11,995 with delivery included.

productNotes.swim-spa: The swim spas on our floor range from the 12 foot J-12 Flow at $30,695, which fits a subdivision yard in Summerside or Hyde Park, to the 19 foot J-19DT PowerPro at $60,895 for a rural lot or a deep Byron ravine yard. The SwimLife SwimFit SwimStream 14 at $38,095 is the budget lane for a triathlete, and the SwimExpert DualStream 19 at $56,095 adds an attached five person hot tub with its own controls. Every model is priced at the sale figure shown, and we manage the crane, the pad drawings and the electrical spec with your contractor.
productNotes.sauna: Clearlight Sanctuary cabins run from the one person Sanctuary 1 at $10,495 to the four seat Sanctuary Retreat at $15,295, and the Sanctuary 2, 3 and Y are the cabins most often paired with a Chill Tubs cold plunge. They suit London basements, spare rooms and attached garages. Serenity outdoor cedar saunas, the Mini at $14,995 and the full Serenity Sauna at $17,495, are built for rural lots and big treed yards, and the heater is sold separately so you can choose electric or wood-burning depending on how far the sauna sits from the panel.
productNotes.cold-plunge: Cold plunges have caught on fast in London, partly because of the Western athletics crowd and partly because hospital shift workers have found that a two minute plunge after a night shift resets the day. Chill Tubs Essential Bath, Essential Pod, Obsidian and Pro are all on the showroom floor at showroom pricing, and we can quote one together with any Clearlight Sanctuary cabin. They need a level spot and a nearby outlet, and they pair with a sauna for a hot and cold routine that fits a Byron backyard or a Westmount basement.

financing: Financing in London tends to follow the calendar. Families in the new subdivisions often finance a tub alongside the deck and fence in the first year in the house, and hospital and university staff on salary like a predictable bi-weekly payment more than a lump sum in the fall. The Nordic Retreat SE shows a bi-weekly figure from $19.38 and the Sport All-In-110V from $15.01, and every Jacuzzi, swim spa and sauna on the site can be quoted the same way. Bring your budget to the Southdale Road West showroom or use the form and we will work out a payment on approved credit that fits.
showroom: Our showroom is at 410 Southdale Road West in Westmount, just off Wonderland Road, with free parking out front and Highway 401 and 402 access a few minutes away. It is the largest hot tub and sauna showroom in Southwestern Ontario: Jacuzzi J-200 through J-500, Nordic, Aquasolus and Wellness Shop Ontario tubs are filled and heated on the floor, the Jacuzzi and SwimLife swim spas are running, and the Clearlight and Serenity saunas are warm. Bring a swimsuit if you want to wet test, and plan on about an hour to get through a shortlist.

The team here has been selling and servicing in London for years and knows the difference between a Byron ravine lot, a Lambeth new build and a Komoka side yard, so you get a straight answer about access and placement. Our London crews deliver and install across the city and out to St. Thomas, Strathroy, Woodstock, Ingersoll, Dorchester, Komoka, Lucan and Ilderton, with Sarnia and Chatham by arrangement. Water testing is free, so bring a sample from your tap or your well and we will set up the start-up chemistry before the tub is filled.

St. Thomas.lead: St. Thomas is half an hour south on Highway 4, a railway town turned commuter and industrial centre with older brick houses on deep lots and new subdivisions filling in on the north and east sides.
body: The older streets off Talbot Street have generous rear yards and detached garages, which makes for an easy dolly delivery and room for a seven seater. The J-385 at $26,595 and the Wellness Shop Ontario S104 at $15,595 both do well here with families who want seats for teenagers and their friends. In the newer subdivisions the lots are tighter and the fence usually goes in the same summer as the tub, so we coordinate with the fence contractor on gate width. St. Thomas is on municipal water, so water care is simple, and if you are on a rural well outside town, bring a sample.

St. Thomas buyers are a mix: plant and trades workers on rotating shifts, hospital staff who commute up to London, and retirees who moved down from the city for a bigger yard. Port Stanley and the Lake Erie shore are twenty minutes further south, so we also see beach and lakeshore owners looking at a Nordic 110V tub or a Serenity Mini for a cottage property. Check with the city on setbacks before pouring a pad, and have a licensed electrician run the circuit with an ESA inspection; we coordinate the timing so the tub is filled the day it lands.
St. Thomas.drive: Take Highway 4 north through Talbotville into Lambeth, then turn east on Southdale Road West and follow it to the showroom near Wonderland Road. About thirty minutes door to door.

Strathroy.lead: Strathroy sits thirty five minutes west along Highway 402, squarely in the snowbelt, with a walkable old downtown, postwar bungalows on wide lots, and new subdivisions on the edges of town.
body: Snow is the story here. Lake-effect bands off Lake Huron run right over Strathroy-Caradoc and the surrounding farms, so a tub in this town gets more cover clearing than one in London proper, and the equipment side should face away from the west wind. We favour full foam Jacuzzi tubs like the J-345 at $23,195 and the J-365 at $24,795 for their heat retention, and we make sure every snowbelt delivery leaves with a cover lifter so nobody is dragging a snow-loaded cover across the deck. Order early in the fall so the pad is poured before the ground freezes.

The town draws commuters who work in London and want land, plus farm families from Mount Brydges, Kerwood and the concessions in between. Farm lots mean space for a Serenity Sauna at $17,495 with a wood-burning heater and a nine seat J-495 at $34,595 for a household that hosts. Many properties outside town are on wells, and Middlesex well water can carry iron, so a fill-day sequestering treatment matters, while Strathroy itself is on municipal water. Check with the municipality on setbacks, and have a licensed electrician handle the circuit and the ESA paperwork.
Strathroy.drive: Take Highway 402 east toward London and exit at Wonderland Road, then head south on Wonderland to Southdale Road West. Allow about thirty five minutes, more when the snow is blowing.

Woodstock.lead: Woodstock is forty five minutes east on Highway 401 at the 403 split, the Oxford County seat, with Victorian streets around the downtown, postwar bungalows, and steady new construction on the north and south ends.
body: Oxford County is dairy country, and Woodstock's housing reflects it: town lots that are wider than London's newer subdivisions, plus farm properties on every concession. Municipal water in Woodstock comes from groundwater and runs hard, so we set most tubs up with a calcium control routine from day one, and rural wells nearby often need the same plus an iron treatment. Families here lean toward seven seaters, and the Jacuzzi J-285 at $18,695 and the Wellness Shop Ontario S106 at $17,695 with its 59 jets and two 6-HP jet pumps are strong picks for the money.

Auto plant and logistics shifts drive a lot of the interest in Woodstock, and a soak at six in the morning after nights is as common as one at nine at night. Farm households with barns and machinery already have heavy electrical service, which makes a J-509 at $39,595 or a full Serenity Sauna with an electric heater straightforward to power. Delivery is by our London crews along the 401, and a rural pad usually takes the truck right to the spot. Check with the city or your Oxford County township for setbacks before the concrete goes in.
Woodstock.drive: Take Highway 401 west for about forty minutes to the Wonderland Road exit, then north on Wonderland to Southdale Road West. The showroom is on Southdale near the Wonderland intersection.

Ingersoll.lead: Ingersoll is thirty minutes east on Highway 401, a compact Oxford County town on the Thames with a historic core, established residential streets, and newer homes on the north side toward the highway.
body: Ingersoll's older lots are deep and narrow, often with a laneway or side drive, which suits a dolly delivery of a six seater like the Jacuzzi J-335 at $21,995 or Aquasolus The Eden at $13,995 with White Glove delivery included. Like Woodstock, the town's municipal supply is groundwater and hard, so plan on a calcium control routine from the first fill. Rural properties toward Thamesford, Putnam and Salford are on wells, so bring a sample and we will test for iron and hardness before your delivery date.

Ingersoll draws plant workers on shifts, farm families, and London commuters who found more house for the money along the 401. Big rural yards mean the Serenity Sauna at $17,495 and a cold plunge fit as easily as a tub, and a swim spa such as the J-16 PowerActive at $46,495 is realistic on a lot where no crane is needed. Setbacks and lot coverage rules differ between the town and the surrounding townships, so check with the municipality that covers your address, and book a licensed electrician early because the good ones fill up in fall.
Ingersoll.drive: Follow Highway 401 west to the Wonderland Road exit, head north on Wonderland and turn onto Southdale Road West. The trip is about half an hour outside of rush hour.

Sarnia.lead: Sarnia is an hour west at the end of Highway 402, where Lake Huron meets the St. Clair River, with lakeshore homes in Bright's Grove, mid century neighbourhoods, and a big shift working population.
body: The lake shapes everything in Sarnia. Wind off Huron is constant along the shore, so a tub in Bright's Grove or Point Edward wants a windbreak, a fence or a corner of the house on its west side, and a cover that seals tight. Lake-effect snow lands here before it reaches Strathroy. We deliver to Sarnia by arrangement and group jobs on the same day, so a little lead time helps. Full foam Jacuzzi models like the J-375 at $25,295 and the J-445 at $27,895 hold heat well in the wind.

Sarnia's buyers are refinery and plant workers on twelve hour rotations, retirees who moved to the lake, and families in the mid century bungalows off Exmouth Street and Indian Road with mature trees and big yards. Twelve hour shifts make a tub or a Clearlight Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 a recovery tool as much as a luxury, and a Chill Tubs Essential beside it suits the cold water crowd who already swim at Canatara in May. Sarnia is on municipal water from the lake, which is easy to care for. Check with the city on setbacks before you pour.
Sarnia.drive: Take Highway 402 east for about an hour to the Wonderland Road exit in London, then south on Wonderland to Southdale Road West. Bright's Grove adds ten minutes at the start.

Dorchester.lead: Dorchester is twenty five minutes east, a Thames Centre village just north of the 401 with half acre and larger lots, a few newer subdivisions, and open farmland in every direction.
body: This is well water country. Most Dorchester properties outside the village core draw from wells, and the water in this part of Middlesex tends to carry iron and hardness, so we test it before delivery and set you up with a sequestering product for fill day. The big lots mean no crane, no narrow gate and room for whatever you want: a nine seat J-495 at $34,595, a Serenity Sauna at $17,495 at the back of the garden, or a 19 foot swim spa where the truck can back right up to the pad.

Dorchester households are commuters who work in London and wanted land, along with farm families who have been on the same concession for generations. Both groups tend to buy for the long haul and pick the tub that will still suit them when the kids are grown, which is why the J-408 at $29,995 and the J-485 at $30,795 do well here. Snow drifts across open fields, so site the tub on the lee side of the house or a hedgerow. Check with Thames Centre on setbacks and permits, and have a licensed electrician run the circuit.
Dorchester.drive: Take Dorchester Road south to Highway 401, go west to the Wonderland Road exit and head north on Wonderland to Southdale Road West. Twenty five minutes most days.

Komoka.lead: Komoka and neighbouring Kilworth are fifteen minutes west of the showroom, a fast growing Middlesex Centre community where new estate subdivisions back onto the Thames valley and Komoka Provincial Park.
body: Komoka lots are a mix of newer executive homes with large rear yards and older village properties on deep lots near the river. The new builds often come with a walkout basement and an unfinished patio area, which is the ideal moment to pour a pad and run the electrical before the landscaping goes in. A six seat J-435 at $27,895 or the J-508L with its lounger at $35,695 fits the scale of these houses, and a Clearlight Sanctuary Y at $13,995 goes into the finished lower level, and with a Chill Tubs Essential beside it makes a full home recovery setup.

Komoka sits at the eastern edge of the snowbelt, so winters here are a little heavier than in Byron ten minutes away, and a cover lifter and a clear path from the back door matter. Part of the community is on municipal water and some properties are still on wells, so tell us which you have. The buyers are young families with London commutes, hospital and university staff who wanted a bigger lot, and a growing number of retirees. Check with Middlesex Centre on setbacks, and plan the fence gate wide enough for a dolly.
Komoka.drive: Take Glendon Drive east, which becomes Oxford Street West as you enter London, then Wonderland Road south to Southdale Road West. About fifteen minutes.

Lucan.lead: Lucan is thirty five minutes north on Highway 4, a Lucan Biddulph village in the heart of the snowbelt with a tidy older core and several newer subdivisions built for London commuters.
body: Lucan gets serious snow. The lake-effect streamers that come off Huron through Grand Bend and Exeter run straight over this stretch of Highway 4, so a tub here is bought with winter in mind: full foam insulation, a heavy cover, a lifter and a placement out of the northwest wind. The Jacuzzi J-355 at $24,795 and the J-365 at $24,795 are both strong choices, and for a farm shop or a first tub the Nordic Retreat SE at $10,195 is easy to run. Get the pad in before Halloween, because frozen ground pushes delivery into spring.

The buyers are young families in the new subdivisions, farmers from the surrounding concessions, and people who work at University Hospital or Western and drive Highway 4 every day. Farm properties have the room and the electrical for a Serenity Sauna at $17,495 and a cold plunge beside it. The village core is on municipal water, the farms are on wells, and Huron and Middlesex county wells can run hard with iron, so bring a sample. Check with Lucan Biddulph on setbacks, and line up a licensed electrician before you book delivery.
Lucan.drive: Head south on Highway 4, which becomes Richmond Street in London, turn west on Fanshawe Park Road to Wonderland Road, then follow Wonderland south all the way to Southdale Road West. About forty minutes.

Ilderton.lead: Ilderton is twenty five minutes northwest, a Middlesex Centre village that has grown quickly with new family subdivisions around an old agricultural core, a short run up Hyde Park Road from London's northwest end.
body: Ilderton's new streets are full of young families who left Hyde Park and Oakridge for a bigger lot, and the tubs that go in are family tubs: the seven seat Jacuzzi J-345 at $23,195, the J-385 at $26,595 or Aquasolus The Calma at $13,995 with seven seats and White Glove delivery included. The lots are big enough for a swim spa too, and the 14 foot J-14 PowerActive at $41,395 is a sensible size for a rear yard that still needs room for a trampoline and a shed.

Ilderton is snowbelt, a little less than Lucan but more than the city, and the open fields west of the village let the wind drive snow onto a cover. Site the tub near the house and keep the cover lifter on the sheltered side. Newer subdivisions are on municipal water while farms on the concessions are on wells, and both are easy once we know which you have. Farm households here also buy Serenity outdoor saunas for the yard. Check with Middlesex Centre on setbacks, and have a licensed electrician handle the circuit.
Ilderton.drive: Take Hyde Park Road south into London, jog over to Wonderland Road and follow it south to Southdale Road West. About twenty five minutes outside of school run traffic.

Byron.lead: Byron is next door to the showroom, a mature west London neighbourhood along the Thames with Boler Mountain, Springbank Park, ravine lots, big maples and some of the most established yards in the city.
body: Byron yards are the classic London setting: a deep lot, a canopy of maples and oaks, sometimes a ravine drop at the back toward the Thames. That means leaf care on the cover every fall, thoughtful placement outside the drip line, and occasionally a crane lift over the house where the side yard is hedged in. Couples in Byron bungalows go for the J-335 at $21,995 or the J-355 at $24,795, and the ski and mountain bike families around Boler Mountain look at a J-408 at $29,995 with room for everyone after a night on the hill.

The neighbourhood is on London municipal water, which is easy to balance, and most homes have panel capacity for a dedicated tub circuit, though a licensed electrician should confirm before you buy. Sloped ravine lots suit a partially sunk swim spa or a Serenity Mini at $14,995 tucked against the grade. Byron residents are five minutes from the showroom, so a water test or a filter swap is a quick errand rather than a trip. Check with the City of London on setbacks for anything close to a fence line or a ravine edge.
Byron.drive: From Commissioners Road West, head to Wonderland Road and go south to Southdale Road West, or take Boler Road south to Southdale and turn east. Five minutes.

productBlurbs.j-509: The J-509 is the tub for a household that hosts, and London has plenty of them in the new walkouts of Sunningdale and Fox Hollow where the patio was poured with a big tub in mind. Eight open seats and 76 jets mean nobody waits for the good spot after a night at Boler Mountain, and ProClarity 6-Stage filtration keeps up with a crowd. At $39,595 it is the top of our floor, and a wet test settles whether you need this much tub.
productBlurbs.j-508: Seven open seats without a lounger suit a family in Talbot Village where the kids bring friends and everyone wants to face each other. Compared with the J-509 you give up one seat and some jets, keep True Water and the same 6-Stage filtration, and save nearly four thousand dollars at $35,695. It sits well on a new build patio with a straight dolly path from the driveway, which most south London lots have.
productBlurbs.j-508l: Couples in Kilworth who bought the executive home with the walkout and want the tub to feel like a treat rather than a pool party pick this one. Six seats and 60 jets at $35,695, the same price as the seven seat J-508, so the jets per person go up rather than the headcount. Fewer seats also means less water to hold warm on a windy January night at the edge of the snowbelt, and True Water keeps the chemistry simple.
productBlurbs.j-408: A household of six in a new Summerside build has been the typical J-408 buyer on our floor for a while. Seven open seats at $29,995 with the J-400 shell and ProClarity 5-Stage filtration handle a family soak on a school night without a lounger taking up room, and the price lands under the J-500 series with much of the same feel. Pair it with a cover lifter, because a new lot has no trees to block the wind yet.
productBlurbs.j-408l: If one person in the house comes home from a twelve hour shift at LHSC needing a full body run of jets, the lounger version of the J-408 is the answer. The J-408L trades one seat for a lounge and 39 jets and holds the same $29,995 price as the open J-408. Six seats still covers a couple with teenagers in Oakridge, and the lounge is the seat people fight over once they have tried it on our floor.
productBlurbs.j-404l: Downsizers in the Masonville condos and townhomes that come with a small terrace or a courtyard need a tub that fits the footprint, and a four seater with a lounge is the one that usually does. The J-404L has 32 jets, a lounge for the person who needs it most, and a compact shell that passes through a standard gate on a dolly. At $25,195 it is the least expensive way into the J-400 series.
productBlurbs.j-495: Nine seats is a farm household outside Ingersoll where the concession road neighbours come over on a Saturday, or a multigenerational family in a Lambeth build with grandparents in the suite. 71 jets keep the whole circle busy, and the open layout lets kids move around. Sale price is $34,595, and a 2025 floor model is on clearance at $31,395 if you want the same nine seats for less. Rural lots take it straight off the truck.
productBlurbs.j-485: Shift workers coming off nights at the Woodstock plants want a tub that heats fast, holds it, and fits seven for the weekend. The J-485 does that with 49 jets and an open layout at $30,795, and the 2025 floor model at $26,295 is the sharpest J-400 deal we have if you can live with last year's colour. It is the open seating sibling of the J-475, so try both and decide whether a lounger matters to you.
productBlurbs.j-475: Couples who run a business from home in Old North and want one lounge seat that does the heavy work while friends fill the other six should look at the J-475 before the open J-485. Same $30,795 sale price, but 55 jets with a lounger instead of 49 in an open circle. The 2025 floor model at $26,295 has been running on our floor all year, which is the best test drive a tub can get.
productBlurbs.j-445: Six open seats at $27,895 puts the J-445 in the middle of the J-400 range, and it is the tub we point Strathroy buyers to when the yard is exposed to the west wind and they want a full foam shell that will not lose ground overnight. 45 jets are enough for a couple with two kids, and the open layout leaves room to stretch out. The 2025 floor model at $23,995 is a strong price for a tub this size.
productBlurbs.j-435: A lounge seat is the first thing a Western varsity athlete asks for, and on a Kilworth executive lot with a walkout the J-435 fits the scale of the house at $27,895. Six seats and 47 jets, with the lounge doing the after-training work, and it shares its price with the open J-445, so the choice comes down to how you like to sit. A 2025 floor model is $24,995 while it lasts.
productBlurbs.j-385: Big families in the St. Thomas subdivisions filling in north of town tend to land on the J-385, because it seats seven with 51 jets at $26,595 and still fits the tighter lots where the fence goes in the same summer. CLEARRAY Active Oxygen keeps the water clear between weekly checks, which matters when the tub sees a lot of teenagers. It is the fullest J-300 and the one to weigh against the J-408 if you are deciding between series.
productBlurbs.j-365: Lucan gets more snow than anywhere else we deliver, and the J-365 is a tub built for that: full foam, seven open seats, 46 jets and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen at $24,795. A commuter family in one of the newer Lucan subdivisions gets seats for everyone and a shell that shrugs off a week of streamers from Lake Huron. Compared with the J-385 you give up five jets and save $1,800, which buys the cover lifter and a good set of steps.
productBlurbs.j-345: For a young family that moved out to Ilderton for the lot size, the J-345 is the sensible seven seater: 41 jets, open seating, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen and ProClear filtration at $23,195. That price gets you the J-300 shell and the Jacuzzi warranty without paying for jets a family of four will not use. The wide new subdivision lots there mean the truck usually backs right to the pad and there is no crane to budget for.
productBlurbs.j-375: Retirees on the Sarnia lakeshore in Bright's Grove buy for two people most nights and six on holidays, and the J-375 serves both with a lounge, 52 jets and a shell that holds heat through a lakeshore winter. At $25,295 it is the J-300 six seater with the most jets, so the person with the sore back gets the best seat in the tub. We deliver to Sarnia by arrangement, so give us a little notice.
productBlurbs.j-355: Couples in Westmount bungalows five minutes from the showroom have made the J-355 one of our steadiest sellers, and the reason is simple: a lounge with 44 jets, seats for four more when family visits, and a $24,795 price that fits a retirement budget. It shares its price with the seven seat J-365, so the decision is a lounger for two versus open seats for seven. Wet test both here on the same afternoon.
productBlurbs.j-335: A Byron couple with a deep treed lot and a habit of a nightly soak under the maples gets everything they need from the J-335: a lounge, 42 jets and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen at $21,995. It is the least expensive J-300 with a lounger, which is why it goes into more established west London yards than any other model we stock. Set it a few feet outside the drip line and the cover stays clean through October.
productBlurbs.j-325: Five open seats and 23 jets is a gentler tub, and the J-325 suits people who want warm water and company more than a massage: a Wortley Village couple who host neighbours on the porch, or grandparents in Old South with visiting grandchildren. At $20,495 it is the way into the J-300 series with True Water and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen, and fewer jets means a quieter pump on a lot where the neighbour's window is close.
productBlurbs.j-315: Downtown London lots along the older streets off Richmond and Dundas can be narrow, with a side gate barely wide enough for a dolly, and the three seat J-315 is the Jacuzzi that fits. A lounge and 23 jets serve a couple who soak every night at $18,795, with CLEARRAY Active Oxygen so water care stays light. Compared with the J-215 you pay $4,700 more for the J-300 shell and True Water.
productBlurbs.j-285: Oxford County dairy families near Woodstock want seven seats at a price that leaves room for the cover lifter, steps and a season of chemicals, and the J-285 delivers that at $18,695 with 42 jets and CLEARRAY UV-C water care. It is the largest J-200 and the closest Jacuzzi in price to our Wellness Shop Ontario S106, so compare the two on the floor. Hard groundwater in Oxford means a calcium routine from the first fill.
productBlurbs.j-245: A first family tub for a house in Hyde Park where the budget also has to cover a fence this year, the J-245 gives you seven open seats and 37 jets at $16,295, the lowest price on a seven seat Jacuzzi. CLEARRAY UV-C handles the water and the ProClassic filter with a ProCatch bag is easy to clean on a Sunday. Sharing a price with the six seat lounger J-235, it is the one to choose when headcount wins.
productBlurbs.j-275: Right now the J-275 is the best value on our floor, because the 2025 units are on clearance from $14,695 and it is a six seater with a lounge and 38 jets. That puts a Jacuzzi with a lounger within reach of a Fanshawe instructor or a St. Thomas plant worker who was looking at a private label tub. Stock is what it is, so if the colour on the floor suits you, claim it before the next weekend.
productBlurbs.j-235: Nurses at St. Joseph's who get home at seven in the morning and want twenty minutes in a lounge before sleep will find the J-235 does that job at $16,295. Six seats, 34 jets, a lounge and CLEARRAY UV-C water care, all in a shell that takes a standard dolly through a Westmount side gate. It is the lounger sibling of the seven seat J-245 at the same price, so the trade is one seat for a full stretch.
productBlurbs.j-225: Commuters who bought in Talbot Village and want a tub before the landscaping is done can start with the J-225: five open seats, 26 jets and CLEARRAY UV-C at $14,695. It is small enough to sit on a temporary gravel pad while the patio is planned and light enough that our crew has it through a gate in minutes. The open layout means nobody argues over a lounger, and the price leaves room for a cover lifter.
productBlurbs.j-215: Beach lots at Port Stanley and Grand Bend have a way of shrinking the usable yard, and a three seat J-215 fits where a six seater will not. A lounge, 21 jets and CLEARRAY UV-C at $14,095 make it the most affordable Jacuzzi we sell, and it heats quickly for a weekend cottage that sits empty midweek. Two people soak comfortably and a third fits when a guest stays over.
productBlurbs.retreat-all-in-110v: A rural shop near Thamesford or a garage in Delaware without a spare breaker is exactly where a Nordic Retreat All-In-110V belongs, because it plugs into a standard 15 amp outlet with the GFCI cord included. Five open seats and 13 jets in a round shell built in Michigan, at $9,195 or from $18.62 bi-weekly OAC. There is no electrician to book and no permit wait, so it can be running the day it lands.
productBlurbs.sport-all-in-110v: At $7,295 the Sport All-In-110V is the least expensive tub on this site and the one we suggest to Fanshawe students sharing a rental in Old East or a first time buyer in a Pond Mills townhome. It plugs into a household outlet, seats five, runs 15 jets and is light enough to move when the lease ends. From $15.01 bi-weekly OAC, and it costs $1,900 less than the Retreat All-In-110V on the same plug and play setup.
productBlurbs.retreat-se: Step up from the plug and play Nordics and the Retreat SE gives a farm family outside Mount Brydges 29 jets on a 220V 40A circuit, which is real massage rather than a warm soak. Five open seats in the round Michigan built shell at $10,195, or from $19.38 bi-weekly OAC. Farm properties already carry the electrical for a barn, so the circuit is a short job, and the round shape sits well on a gravel pad beside a drive shed.
productBlurbs.ontario-s106: Our own Ontario S106 is the tub we sell to Strathroy families who want seven seats and serious jet power without a Jacuzzi price: 59 jets driven by two 6-HP pumps, a 50 square foot flow-through filter and Thermal Shield insulation for a snowbelt January, at $17,695. It is built in the USA and sits on the floor beside the J-285, which costs $1,000 more with 42 jets, so the comparison is easy to make in person.
productBlurbs.ontario-s104: Growing families in the north end of St. Thomas usually want seven seats first and everything else second, and the Ontario S104 answers that at $15,595 with 54 jets, two 6-HP pumps and a flow-through filter. Thermal Shield insulation keeps the hydro bill flat on an open subdivision lot. Compared with the S106 you give up five jets and the larger filter and save $2,100, which is most of a cover lifter and steps.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s103: A Woodstock auto plant shift ends with a sore back, and the Ontario L S103 puts a lounger in a six seat USA built tub at $15,595 with 51 jets and two 6-HP pumps behind them. Ozone water care and Thermal Shield insulation are standard, and the flow-through filter is simple to rinse. It shares its price with the seven seat S104, so the choice is a lounge for you or an extra seat for the neighbours.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s105: Hospital residents renting in Old North before they buy tend to want a tub they can set from the keypad without reading a manual, and the Ontario L S105 has the GECKO K1000 control on a six seat lounger tub with 56 jets and two 6-HP pumps at $17,695. It is the most equipped tub in the Ontario series, and Thermal Shield insulation keeps it warm through a shift week when nobody is home to check it.
productBlurbs.the-brook: Four seats and 23 jets in a European built shell at $10,995, with White Glove delivery and setup included, makes The Brook the tub for a Kilally townhouse or a downsizer in a Masonville condo with a ground floor patio. Ozone water care keeps the routine light for someone who travels. Delivery included matters more than it sounds, because a tight townhouse gate is where delivery quotes usually climb, and here there is nothing to add.
productBlurbs.the-cove: Seven open seats for $11,995 is the number that gets a Summerside family with three kids into a full size tub, and The Cove includes White Glove delivery and setup worth up to $1,900 on top. 27 jets keep it gentle, which suits a tub used more for family time than deep massage. It is built in Europe by Superior Wellness, and it is the entry to seven seats on this site, below even The Calma in the same brand.
productBlurbs.the-calma: Ilderton families who left the city for a bigger lot and want seven seats plus real jet count look at The Calma: 37 jets, open seating, ozone water care and White Glove delivery and setup at $13,995. That is ten more jets than The Cove for $2,000 more, which is where most buyers land once they have sat in both. A new subdivision lot with no trees yet means the truck backs right up to the pad.
productBlurbs.the-eden: One person in an Ingersoll household who does physical work all day gets the lounger, and The Eden makes that seat the point: six seats, 42 jets and a lounge at $13,995 with White Glove delivery and setup included. Same price as The Calma, so it is a lounger for six against open seats for seven. Ingersoll's hard municipal water means a calcium routine from the first fill, and the ozone system helps between checks.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-powerpro: A Dorchester lot with a half acre and a truck path to the pad is where a 19 foot dual temperature swim spa makes the most sense, and the J-19DT PowerPro is the top of that list at $60,895. The swim end runs cool for a triathlete training through February, the hot tub end runs warm for everyone else, and 53 jets with quad 50 square foot filtration keep up with both. Two circuits, one 20A and one 40A, so plan the electrical early.
productBlurbs.j-19-powerpro: Masters swimmers who train at the Western pool and want the strongest current on the site should be looking at the J-19 PowerPro at $58,995. Nineteen feet, four seats and 34 jets, with the PowerPro swim system and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen plus dual 50 square foot filters. It runs on a single 40A circuit, unlike the dual temperature J-19DT PowerPro which needs two. A deep Old North rear yard takes it with a crane lift planned from the street.
productBlurbs.j-16-powerpro: Sixteen feet is the length that fits a Byron ravine lot with a deck on one side and still gives a serious swimmer a full stroke, and the J-16 PowerPro at $54,295 carries the same PowerPro current and 34 jets as the 19 foot version in a footprint the crane can drop between the maples. Four seats and dual 50 square foot filters. It is the right pick when the yard, not the swimmer, is the limit.
productBlurbs.j-14-powerpro: Physiotherapy patients working through a knee or a hip, and spouses who mostly want a hot tub, end up in the J-14 PowerPro more than any other PowerPro, because 14 feet gives a real walking and jogging lane and 51 jets across five seats make it a therapy tub afterward. At $48,795 it fits an Oakridge rear yard on a reinforced slab. Talk to your physio about the routine and we will match the current setting to it.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-poweractive: Families in Lucan with a big new lot who want the kids in a pool and the adults in a hot tub at the same time get both in the J-19DT PowerActive at $53,295, with separate swim and hot tub zones, six seats and 51 jets. It costs $7,600 less than the J-19DT PowerPro and uses the PowerActive swim system rather than PowerPro, which most families never miss. Four 50 square foot filters handle the crowd, and it needs a 20A and a 40A circuit.
productBlurbs.j-19-poweractive: Runners and cyclists in Riverbend working through an injury do not need a racing current, they need a long lane at walking to easy swimming pace, and the J-19 PowerActive at $51,395 gives them 19 feet of it with four seats and 32 jets for the cool down. CLEARRAY Active Oxygen with dual 50 square foot filters keeps the water simple, and the single 40A circuit keeps the electrical quote reasonable. Rural lots take it without a crane.
productBlurbs.j-16-poweractive: Sixteen feet on a single 40A circuit at $46,495 makes the J-16 PowerActive the swim spa we quote most for established Oakridge Acres and Westmount lots where the yard is deep but the gate is on the narrow side and the crane has to come over the house. Four seats and 32 jets, the same as the 19 foot PowerActive, in a shorter shell that is easier to lift. A family that swims for fitness rather than sport is the buyer.
productBlurbs.j-14-poweractive: At $41,395 the J-14 PowerActive is the swim spa for a Talbot Village or Ilderton rear yard that still needs room for a trampoline and a shed. Fourteen feet with a walking to easy swim current, five seats with 49 jets, so it doubles as the family hot tub every night it is not used for laps. One 40A circuit and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen with dual 50 square foot filters. A reinforced slab on London clay is the base.
productBlurbs.j-13-powerplay: Eight seats in 13 feet tells you what the J-13 PowerPlay is for: a Hyde Park family that wants a pool to splash in and a tub to soak in, and is not training for anything. At $33,195 with 38 jets and a single 32A circuit it fits a subdivision yard that a 16 footer would swallow. It is the bigger of the two PowerPlay models, and the one we suggest when there are three or more kids in the house.
productBlurbs.j-12-flow: The shortest swim spa on the site at 12 feet, the J-12 Flow at $30,695 is the answer for newer south London lots in Summerside where the yard is 30 feet deep and a deck already takes half of it. Eight seats and 31 jets make it a large hot tub with a gentle current for water walking, and CLEARRAY UV-C with a 50 square foot DFML filter keeps care simple. One 32A circuit, and usually no crane.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-dualstream-19: A Komoka executive lot with a walkout and room for two things gets both in one shell with the SwimLife SwimExpert DualStream 19: a 19 foot swim lane with 53 jets and four seats, plus an attached five person hot tub with 30 jets and its own controls. At $56,095 against a $74,995 regular price it is the deepest markdown on the swim spa floor. ClearStream mineral based water care keeps the chemistry gentle for daily use after a long shift.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-aquastream-17: Seventeen feet is a length Jacuzzi does not offer, and for a Warbler Woods lot that is a couple of feet too short for a 19 footer the SwimLife SwimExpert AquaStream 17 at $50,095 is the fit. Three seats, 30 jets and the AquaStream current on a single 40A circuit, with ClearStream mineral based water care. It is the single temperature alternative to the DualStream 19 for a household that swims more than it soaks.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-swimstream-14: Nurses on rotating shifts at University Hospital who want a swim before bed at eight in the morning need a spa that runs quietly and heats reliably, and the SwimLife SwimExpert SwimStream 14 at $44,795 does that in 14 feet with three seats and 30 jets on a 32A circuit. ClearStream mineral based water care suits daily use. Against the SwimFit SwimStream 14 you pay $6,700 more for the SwimExpert current and two extra jets.
productBlurbs.swimfit-aquastream-17: A Sarnia retiree with a Bright's Grove lot who wants to keep swimming after the Canatara season ends gets 17 feet for $43,795 in the SwimLife SwimFit AquaStream 17. Three seats, 28 jets, a 40A circuit and ClearStream mineral based water care, in a shell built for daily fitness swimming rather than racing. We group Sarnia deliveries, so a few weeks of notice lets the crane and the crew arrive together.
productBlurbs.swimfit-swimstream-14: At $38,095 the SwimLife SwimFit SwimStream 14 is the lowest priced true swim lane on the site, and the model we suggest to a triathlete renting a house near Western who plans to take it to the next property. Fourteen feet, three seats, 28 jets and a 32A circuit, with ClearStream mineral based water care. It moves on a flatbed without a crane on most lots, which matters when you are not staying forever.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-1: A resident coming off nights at Victoria Hospital who wants twenty minutes of heat before sleep and has one corner of a Wortley Village basement to give up is the Sanctuary 1 buyer. One seat, full spectrum infrared on a household circuit, $10,495 with an AROMA ONE aromatherapy diffuser included. It assembles in an afternoon and fits under the low ceilings common in Old South houses, which is the first thing to measure.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-2: Couples in Byron bungalows who converted the spare room pick the Sanctuary 2, because two seats side by side at $11,795 is the size that gets used every evening rather than admired. Full spectrum infrared heats you rather than the room, so a January session in a cold basement still works, and it runs on a standard household circuit like the Sanctuary 1. Add a Chill Tubs plunge beside it and the room becomes a contrast setup.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-3: Three seats at $12,995 makes the Sanctuary 3 the cabin for a Fanshawe coaching household or a family in Stoney Creek in north London where two teenagers train and both want in after practice. Full spectrum infrared with True Wave heaters and the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters, in Basswood or Mahogany. It needs a bit more floor space than the Sanctuary 2, so bring the room dimensions to the showroom.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-5: The Sanctuary 5 seats five, the most of any indoor Clearlight cabin, priced at $13,995, and it is the one to sit in if the three person Sanctuary 3 felt tight when you tried it. Full spectrum True Wave heaters and the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters come with it, and it suits a finished lower level in the newer Masonville houses where ceiling height is not the problem it is downtown. Sit in both cabins on our floor before deciding.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-y: Four seats at $13,995 puts the Sanctuary Y at the same price as the five seat Sanctuary 5, so a Komoka family with a walkout basement chooses on which cabin fits the room rather than on price. Full spectrum infrared with True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, and the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters. The Y is the cabin we most often quote alongside a Chill Tubs plunge for the lower level, each priced on its own.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-c: A Sunningdale house with a home gym already in the basement is where the Sanctuary C goes: four seats, full spectrum infrared, True Wave heaters and a shape that tucks into the corner beside the treadmill. At $14,495 it costs $500 more than the Sanctuary Y for a layout that uses a corner rather than a wall. Lifetime warranty on the cabin and heaters, and it is heated on our floor so you can compare the two.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-retreat: Farm households outside Lucan with a big finished basement and four people who all want in after chores get the Sanctuary Retreat, the top of the Clearlight range at $15,295 with four seats and full spectrum True Wave heaters. Basswood or Mahogany, lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters, and enough room that nobody's knees touch. It is the cabin to weigh against a Serenity cedar sauna if you have the yard for either.
productBlurbs.serenity-mini: A Serenity Mini fits the corner of a Byron garden between the maple and the fence, and at $14,995 in knotty cedar it is the way into a real Canadian made hot sauna that runs up to 194 degrees. Choose an electric heater if the panel is close or wood if the sauna sits at the back of a rural lot, since the heater is sold separately either way. Clear cedar is available for a cleaner grain.
productBlurbs.serenity-sauna: The full size Serenity Sauna at $17,495 in knotty cedar belongs on a farm lot near Dorchester with a woodpile and no desire to trench a circuit to the far end of the property, because a wood-burning heater turns it into a proper hot sauna with nothing to plug in. Canadian made, up to 194 degrees, open bench seating and clear cedar available. Heater sold separately, so budget for electric or wood at the showroom.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-bath: Western athletes who already know cold water from the training room want the simplest version at home, and the Chill Tub Essential Bath is that: a bath style plunge that sits beside a Clearlight cabin in a Westmount basement or on a patio near a Serenity. Pricing is at the showroom, where all four Chill Tubs models are running so you can put an arm in first. Pair it with any sauna we sell for a contrast routine.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-pod: A pod shape takes less floor space than a bath, which is what a Wortley Village couple with a small finished basement needs when the sauna already claims one wall. The Chill Tub Essential Pod is the compact entry to the range, priced at the showroom, and it needs only a level spot and a nearby outlet. Shift workers at St. Joseph's use a two minute plunge after nights to reset the clock, and the Pod is the one most of them choose.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-obsidian: For a Riverbend house where the plunge will sit on the patio year round and needs to look like it belongs there, the Chill Tub Obsidian is the dark finished model in the range. Showroom pricing applies, and it is set up on our floor beside the Sanctuary cabins. A Boler Mountain ski family uses it after a night on the hill the same way the athletes do after practice, sauna first and then two minutes cold.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-pro: The Chill Tub Pro sits at the top of the Chill Tubs range, for someone who has kept a cold routine long enough to want the full size unit, which in London usually means a masters swimmer, a Fanshawe strength coach or a hockey family in Ilderton. Priced at the showroom only. It goes beside a Serenity or a Clearlight in a yard or basement, and our team walks you through placement, drainage and the outlet it needs.
productBlurbs.summit-ws190: Twelve hour rotations at the Sarnia refineries end in a chair, and the Wellness Shop Summit WS190 is the higher of our two massage chairs for exactly that: a full body session you can run every night without leaving the house. Pricing is at the showroom, and the only way to judge a massage chair is to sit in it for ten minutes, which is why both chairs are plugged in and ready on Southdale Road West.
productBlurbs.dreamcatcher-ws170: A Westmount retiree who wants a chair in the family room rather than a tub in the yard should try the Wellness Shop Dreamcatcher WS170, the second of our two massage chairs, with pricing at the showroom. It suits a house where the yard is shaded and small and the money goes to something used daily indoors. Sit in it and the Summit WS190 back to back on our floor, because the difference is felt, not read.
productBlurbs.duke-series: Snow off Lake Huron piles on a Strathroy tub cover several times a week in January, and an enclosed Visscher Duke Series gazebo takes that job away entirely. Western red cedar in a veranda style enclosure, several sizes, showroom pricing. It turns a tub into a room you use in a February whiteout, and it keeps maple keys off the water on a treed lot too. Bring your tub footprint and we will size it.
productBlurbs.cypress-series: Cedar panel construction on the Visscher Cypress Series gives a Woodstock backyard privacy from the neighbours on the sides that need it, which is the balance most subdivision lots want. Western red cedar, multiple sizes, priced at the showroom. It suits a tub on an open new lot where the fence is still going in, and it sets the tub in a defined space rather than in the middle of the lawn.
productBlurbs.hudson-series: An enclosed Visscher Hudson Series at 11 by 14 and up gives a Kilworth family a year round tub room with walls and a roof, which on the eastern edge of the snowbelt means the cover stays dry and the deck stays clear. Western red cedar, showroom pricing, and sized from 11 by 14 upward for a full size Jacuzzi with room to walk around it. We can set the gazebo on the same slab as the tub when the pad is poured.
productBlurbs.sequoia-11-14: Louvered roof slats on the Visscher Sequoia 11×14 let you set how much sun reaches the deck, which suits a Byron patio under the maples where you want light in April and shade in July. Western red cedar in an open-air design at 11 by 14 feet, showroom pricing. It fits over a seven seat tub with space around it, and it looks right beside the mature landscaping of an established west London yard.
productBlurbs.sedona-9-9: Nine by nine is the footprint for a Pond Mills or White Oaks townhouse yard where a four or five seat tub sits against the fence and there is no room for a larger structure. The Visscher Sedona 9×9 is open-air western red cedar, priced at the showroom, and it frames a J-315 or a Nordic round tub without crowding the rest of the patio.
